brief: GS's Privorotsky reads a Fed hike from hawkish governor Warsh (framed as removing accommodation, tied to commodities/energy/geopolitics) as pulling forward total priced tightening rather than adding to it, leaving October odds near 50/50; equities sold off and the front end repriced but the back end held, and when oil eased and the 10-year slipped back below 5% sentiment turned constructive again. The BOE held at 3.75% on a hawkish 6-3 vote and lifted its inflation view above 4% for early next year, but paused gilt sales for six months, a QT offset that helped global duration. The BOJ hiked to a 31-year high but two dovish dissents weakened the yen. Oil diplomacy (Iran/China, Iran/Saudi) points to de-escalation ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting he calls critical. On AI, Anthropic's Claude now does 26% of its own R&D with an unclear automation trajectory, while GPU price hikes at Nebius and CoreWeave argue compute stays scarce even if buildout undershoots forecasts. Given AAII's -24.5 bull/bear spread (lowest since May 2025) and depressed Fear & Greed, he calls the pessimism an overreaction that should force re-risking, while flagging Russia/NATO drone incursions as a secondary tail he's hedging.
